title: Bounded flat constructible total tensor on the etale site
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]). Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$ be integers. Let $P,Q$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes of these sheaves, with flat constructible terms, with $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ and $Q^j=0$ for $j\notin[c,d]$. Flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] means that tensoring with the term is exact; constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] means locally constant with finite $A$-module values on each stratum of a finite constructible locally closed stratification. Form the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{A_X}Q)$, with $T^n=\bigoplus_{i+j=n}P^i\otimes_{A_X}Q^j$ and differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_Q$ on bidegree $(i,j)$. Then $T$ has flat constructible terms, is zero outside $[a+c,b+d]$, and every cohomology sheaf of $T$ is constructible. It is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] (tensoring an acyclic complex with it gives an acyclic total tensor), and its image in the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is isomorphic to the relative derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] of the images of $P$ and $Q$. For every $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero, $T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}N$ has cohomology only in $[a+c,b+d]$. The zero ring, zero terms, degenerate intervals and empty scheme are allowed.

proof.text: Use braiding to turn the given exact tensorRight functors into categorical flat objects. Tensor products of flat objects are flat by composition of exact tensor functors. Finite biproducts of flat objects are flat: apply the source closedUnderLimitsOfShape_discrete_flat to the finite product cone of the biproduct. All these constructions remain in the stated category of etale sheaves valued in ModuleCat A; there is no conversion to SheafOfModules.

The coproduct universal property identifies the degree-n total term [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] with the finite coproduct of P^i tensor Q^(n-i), indexed by i in the integer interval [a,b]. Construct the two inverse maps using mapBifunctorDesc and the summand inclusions. Terms with i outside [a,b] vanish because tensorRight preserves zero. This is the proved private bounded_total_term_iso. The finite biproduct comparison and the preceding flatness facts give flatness of every total term. If n<a+c or n>b+d then every summand has a zero factor; the source isStrictlyGE_tensorObj and isStrictlyLE_tensorObj implement precisely this calculation.

source.place: Proof (1),(2), finite A: bounded total tensor of the two models; elementary degree calculation

proof.text: Convert finite-value constructibility to the source predicate using [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. Apply the already proved Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.tensorObj to each tensor summand. Its proof is the fibre-product common-refinement argument: [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] and [lemma-constructible-of-refines] make both restrictions finite locally constant, the source monoidal etale pullback comparison carries tensor to the strata, and [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-locally-constant-part] and [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-finite-part] give finite local constancy of their tensor. The source IsConstructibleSheaf.biproduct theorem, deduced from the split-extension case of [thm-constructible-serre], gives constructibility of the finite sum and hence of each total term.

proof.text: For every degree n apply the kernel clause of [thm-constructible-serre] to the outgoing differential of the short complex T.sc n. Its cyclesIsKernel comparison makes the cycles constructible. Apply the cokernel clause to the map from the previous term into these cycles, and use homologyIsCokernel to obtain constructible homology. The homologyFunctorFactors comparison of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] identifies this homology object with H^n(Q(T)). Convert back with [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison].

source.place: Tag 03RZ, lemma-constructible-abelian, clause (3); finite sums and cohomology are the displayed elementary deductions

proof.text: The upper support bounds and flat terms permit the generic source criterion [lem-sfb-bounded-above-flat-kflat], CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat, for P and T. Its categorical K-flatness predicate is definitionally the two-sided quasi-isomorphism predicate [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] in the conclusion. The existing generic source comparison QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft (recorded by [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], here specialized to the etale sheaf category rather than its module-category example) gives Q(P) tensor-derived Q(Q) isomorphic to Q(T). Reverse it. This is the same derived tensor as [def-kun-derived-tensor], whose source definition is curriedTensor on this monoidal derived category.

source.place: Tags 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction

proof.text: Apply the existing source theorem [lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude], DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat, to T with support interval [a+c,b+d] and the flatness proved above. For every arbitrary sheaf N in degree zero it gives both cohomological bounds. The isGE_iff and isLE_iff characterizations give exactly the required vanishing of derived cohomology outside this interval. Thus the single-sheaf computation is reused in the actual coefficient category without the separate independent-universe ringed-site comparison.
